processing_steps.method: air induction melting with flux cover (AIMFC)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 40-kg melt; protective flux cover of Al2O3, CaO, MgO and CaF2; top poured into split cast iron molds.

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled Fe-7Al-0.35C plate with an Fe3Al matrix and Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates; the precipitates form semi-continuous stringers along grain boundaries plus intragranular particles, and the grains are slightly elongated.

phases_present.morphology: semi-continuous stringers along grain boundaries plus intragranular particles

precipitates.distribution: semi-continuous stringers along grain boundaries plus intragranular particles

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify and confirm the Fe3Al matrix and Fe3AlC0.5 precipitate phases.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe3Al and Fe3AlC0.5 peaks observed; similar peaks observed in alloys with carbon 0.35–1 wt.%.

characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the hot-rolled microstructure and precipitate distribution.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.35 wt.% C plate: dark precipitates form semi-continuous stringers along grain boundaries plus intragranular particles; grains slightly elongated.

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of Fe-7Al-0.35C (Table IV): Al 6.78, Si 0.19, Mn 0.15, S 0.004, C 0.35 wt.% [b0052].
The volume fraction of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates increases significantly with increasing carbon content [b0061].
The increase in bulk hardness with increasing carbon (Table V) suggests precipitation hardening by hard Fe3AlC0.5 is the predominant strengthening mechanism in these alloys [b0062].

The addition of carbon to Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy resulted in significant improvement in room-temperature strength (396–610 MPa), while room-temperature tensile elongation decreases significantly (18–3%) with increasing carbon content [b0062].

Fe-7 wt.% Al alloys are not susceptible to environmental embrittlement; the decrease in room-temperature ductility with increasing carbon is attributed solely to the increase in volume fraction of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates [b0062].

Table V and Fig. 5 captions label the carbon-series route 'AIM', whereas the section text (b0060) states the alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC) [b0053,b0055,b0060].
